title: Debugging a $4 Trading Bot: It Made Money on the Spread and Still Lost
author: wut_wut_spez
selftext:
Quick context on the stakes, since they're tiny: this bot was trading with about five dollars. It's tuition money; I want the bugs to be cheap. Small stakes make this a good post-mortem. Every mistake here would look the same with a zero or two added. It would just hurt more.



The code is public: github.com/blakelapierre/crypto-mm-public. Every spec I quote below is in docs/specs/.



What the bot was supposed to do

The "ladder" bot was a market maker on Coinbase. The idea is simple. For each coin, you rest one buy order a little below the market and one sell order a little above it. When someone trades against you on both sides, you keep the gap between them (the spread). All orders are post-only, so the bot always adds liquidity, and at my fee tier that meant paying 0.35% instead of 0.75%. A scanner picked which coins to trade by ranking recent volatility, and a rotation loop swapped coins in and out as things changed.



On paper: collect spreads, pay small fees, repeat.
